title: The First iPhone and the Renaming That Became 'iPhone OS' (2007)
explainer: When Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPhone on January 9, 2007, he described it on stage as running a version of 'OS X'; by the time it shipped that June, Apple had renamed the operating system 'iPhone OS,' which wasn't renamed again to iOS until 2010. Every native app you build with SwiftUI today runs on a direct descendant of that first, strictly single-purpose phone operating system.

title: Swift's Origins as Chris Lattner's Side Project (2010-2014)
explainer: Apple engineer Chris Lattner began designing Swift as a personal project in July 2010, years before it became public, with most of Apple's own app teams unaware it existed until shortly before its unveiling at WWDC in June 2014. That a modern, memory-safer systems language could be built quietly inside one engineer's project and then replace Objective-C as Apple's primary language within a few years is a useful data point for how fast platform-level language change can actually happen.
